entry_points.text: Stopper threads are per-CPU self-parking hotplug threads bound to the stop class with early lock and queue init; priority set validates class and clamps niceness across process, group or user.
Triple queries copy translated real, effective and saved identities in order; pid family returns group, thread and user or group ids.
Times entries fill user, system and inherited times then report wall clock.
Job control moves leaders to groups and queries group identifiers with zero meaning caller, reporting missing targets and permission problems.

exports.text: Stack service formats captured addresses with decoding into caller buffers reporting full length, and captures register-anchored kernel or current-user stacks honouring skip counts.
Single and paired CPU execution queues one callback with caller identity, waiting on sync forms and returning immediately on nowait, reporting absence or callback status.
Global and core-scoped stop runs a callback across target CPUs under hotplug exclusion; core form uses the sibling mask and requires the hotplug lock.
Identity helpers change real, effective, saved and filesystem user and group with wrappers forwarding; session creation reports the new id and UTS control wakes poll waiters.

hazards.text: Missing address array warns and yields no output; stop callbacks run atomic and must not sleep, with parked work warning on lifecycle violation.

Unknown classes report invalid argument and empty matches report not found; nproc excess only marks the task for later enforcement; unwritable destinations or allocation failures fail without state change.
Stack, stop, priority and accounting paths rely on external per-CPU, list, bug-warning, RCU, locking, scheduler, atomic and interrupt helpers owned elsewhere.

invariants.text: Bounded collector satisfies skip first, stores within capacity and reports continuability, dropping scheduler addresses in nosched form; inaccessible stacks yield empty with pinning, legacy adapters bridge descriptors, IRQ lists truncate after entry-text hit.
Diagnostics emit only for a CPU stopper thread naming callback and caller; stops from inactive CPUs busy-wait for the mutex, run local work inline and combine statuses.
Priority change allowed on user match or capability, lowering needs extra capability and security approval; first error kept while remaining targets still attempted.
User hash lookup by id under spinlock with interrupts saved returns referenced entry or null; allocation initializes refcount and limits then rechecks under lock to drop duplicates or link newcomer.
All-ones leaves a field unchanged; moves compare against old identities or need privilege, filesystem follows effective, real-user moves refresh accounting and defer nproc excess to a flag.

Group moves default zeroes, reject negatives and session leaders, require same-session pre-exec targets and existing groups plus approval; session setup rebinds, detaches terminal and notifies after unlock.

Uname snapshots shared identity under shared semaphore then rewrites release and machine; hostname install takes exclusive, needs admin privilege, checks length, mixes randomness, pads and notifies; queries truncate with copies outside.

locks.text: Global stop mutex with progress flag backs off contended two-CPU queues; two-CPU path locks stoppers in CPU order, validates enabled and enqueues atomically; queue drained under per-CPU lock with interrupts disabled.
Group and session changes hold tasklist exclusive interrupt-disabled inside RCU with queries using RCU only; priority set and query add tasklist read handling.

state_machines.text: Coordinated stop advances idle, prepare, disable-interrupts, run and exit with acks; workers preserve flags, disable interrupts in disable phase, run callback on active members and suppress stall reports while waiting.

Credential update validates, allocates a copy, applies gated changes, checks security then installs or discards; accounting returns on hit else allocates and links or adopts winner; group rebinding stages releases, changes under exclusion then frees.

structs.text: Stack collector pairs array, capacity, skip quota and retained count; stop uses completion with count and status, per-CPU stopper with thread, lock, queue and diagnostics, plus descriptor with callback, counts, mask, phase and acks.

Credentials carry four user and four group identities with accounting and namespace; user accounting carries identity, refcount, hash node and limits; time reports use thread-group plus inherited child fields.

Overflow user, group and filesystem identities have defaults with sysctl exposure; arch process-control fallbacks for alignment, float, endian, TSC, vector, auth, tagged, RISC-V and DEXCR report invalid argument.
